sources.read_finding: The source describes clean profiling and an input-length-conditioned threshold, while the mitigation discussion reports padding overhead. sources.read_finding: Appendix D directly reports attack accuracy under fixed/random packet padding, with 20 traces per prompt at temperature 0.8 and a maximum 8.7x token-payload overhead. It does not state that the classifier was refit on padded traces for those table cells or identify shared held-out trace IDs across no-padding/padding conditions. Both bindings remain open.

sources.paper_locator: 4.3 lines 236-251; 5.1.2 lines 326-337; Table 1 lines 264-280; Appendix E.3 lines 749-751
sources.read_finding: The source explicitly distinguishes real-time online execution from post-hoc offline modification and provides Table 1 detector/task-accuracy rows. It does not expose episode IDs showing that raw and humanized detector outcomes were scored on the same held-out episodes. This supports the mode distinction but not R5 matched-test binding.

Paper states an 8:1:1 sample-disjoint split for primary attack evaluation and describes random selected-token replacement as a mitigation at inference. It does not say whether the attack model for Table 4 was retrained under each replacement condition or that the same test IDs were used for baseline and mitigation. No cell is closed.

sources.paper_locator: VII-B dataset/protocol and VII-C results; IX-A to IX-B1 lines 370-387

Source is accessible, but the needed empirical bindings are not reported at the cited mitigation scope.
